analysis:
The supplied change to docs/architecture/inference.md adds documentation only (head lines 956-989): an excluded shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup) that runs before the calibration probes for ordinary EngineV2 slots. It describes a 128-token greedy cold-cache detection probe, then a solo prompt and a served-width cell, with a 20-second wall budget. No probe trains a rate or counter. Preemption leaves the attempt due, while a timeout or refusal completes it. The startup preload warms each loaded model before registration, or before a standalone listener opens.

The two units are base-side text of the same file, and the patch excerpt is truncated at the final sentence. The base text is surrounding context, not new behavior. I could not see the head implementation, so I could not verify the described behavior.

Security relevance is limited. The warmup is a local, self-generated workload with no consumer plaintext. It does not touch the prefix cache (T-041), the coordinator contract (TB-002) or attestation. I did not see warmup state leaking consumer data, and it does not alter authorization, encryption or at-rest artifacts.

Open integration questions: whether warmup synthetic prompts could populate the SSD prefix cache (T-041) or leave residual GPU or KV state (T-028), and whether the warmup can delay registration or serving enough to matter for availability (T-029). The documentation says these probes are excluded from training. The warmup does not appear to alter cache salting or the account-scoped isolation of coordinator-authored cacheSalt. If code accompanies this doc, a reviewer should confirm that warmup requests bypass prefix donation. This is a documentation-only observation, with no finding to report.
